report:
**Conclusion:** Your understanding is correct—the claim that food-grade wax coatings on apples cause cancer is false. Food safety experts and scientific evidence confirm that these edible coatings are non-carcinogenic and safe for consumption.

### Key Evidence

* **FDA Approval and Safety:** Commercial waxes used on apples—such as carnauba wax, beeswax, and shellac—are approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and are not considered carcinogenic (https://www.fertilehope.org/can-eating-waxed-apples-cause-cancer/). 
* **Indigestible Nature:** Food-grade apple wax is indigestible, meaning it passes through the human digestive system without being absorbed into the body (https://wellnd.com/is-wax-coating-on-apples-safe).
* **Functional Purpose:** Apples produce a natural wax coating that gets washed off during post-harvest processing to clean dirt and chemicals. Food-grade wax is reapplied in minute amounts strictly to prevent moisture loss, maintain freshness, and inhibit mold (https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/wax-on-apples-causes-cancer/).
* **Debunked Myth:** Academic research and fact-checkers categorize the idea that apple wax harbors carcinogens or poses health risks as a persistent food myth spread by online misinformation (https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/wax-on-apples-causes-cancer/, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950329323002185).
